name: New Born — Newborn beyond the 31-day eligibility period: deny the claim
description: Nine guided steps, one per row of the 281.1 document's table plus the reject-code entry: identify the PX_281 hard edit, verify the patient's NH state, check the event hierarchy, note the 10/20/2026 date of service and the 09/14/2026 date of birth, find no member record for the newborn on Search → Member, measure the service date against the 31-day newborn window, deny the claim with the reject code and submit the Deny decision.

steps.name: Identify the 281 hard edit
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab. The app displays all the edits on the claim, with the 281 hard edit highlighted with an error indication — this is the current event to resolve. PX_281 (NEWBORN OVER 31/60/61 DAYS OLD) is the out-of-window newborn event: it fires when the newborn's date of service falls outside the enrollment window the member's state grants.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Event Resolution tab is opened while this step is active. The workspace opens on this tab, and a click on the tab the trainee is already standing on still records a visit.
steps.hint: On 'Event Resolution', the Active Edit section shows Edit Code PX_281 with a Hard Edit badge, and All Edits lists it first, in red.

steps.name: Verify the patient's state
steps.description: Open the Member Info tab and verify the state associated with the patient, in the State field of the Patient section. The state matters because it sets how long the newborn enrollment window runs — the edit name itself names three lengths, 31, 60 and 61 days. In this scenario the state is NH, so the window is 31 days and the trainee proceeds.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Member Info tab is opened while this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Member Info', read the State field under Patient. It reads NH, so the newborn window is 31 days.

steps.name: Check the event hierarchy
steps.description: Return to the Event Resolution tab and review the full events list to determine whether any other event must be resolved before Event 281, following the established event hierarchy. If other events are present that precede it, resolve those first according to the hierarchy; if none do, proceed. Here the claim carries seven events, but none of the other six precedes 281 in the hierarchy, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Event Resolution tab is opened again while this step is active. Step 2 moved the trainee to Member Info, so this is a real tab change.
steps.hint: On 'Event Resolution', read the All Edits list top to bottom. Only PX_281 is active; nothing above it in the hierarchy is outstanding.

steps.name: Note the Date of Service
steps.description: Open the Claim Lines tab and determine the Date of Service (DOS) on which the services were rendered. The claim has two lines; both were rendered on the same day. In this scenario the DOS is 10/20/2026.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Claim Lines tab is opened while this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Claim Lines', read the From date and To on each of the two lines: both read 10/20/2026.

steps.name: Note the patient's Date of Birth
steps.description: Return to the Member Info tab and verify the patient's Date of Birth (DOB) in the Patient section. In this scenario the DOB is 09/14/2026. You will measure the date of service against this date.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Member Info tab is opened again while this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Member Info', read Date Of Birth (DOB) under Patient: 09/14/2026.
steps.checklistItem: Note the patient's Date of Birth

steps.name: Search for the newborn's member record
steps.description: Open the Search tab and its Member sub-tab to check whether a member record exists for the newborn. The system has already searched automatically for the patient on the claim: the Member ID, First name, Last name and DOB on the Search Member form are auto-filled. If member information is found, the newborn is enrolled and the claim follows standard claim processing guidelines; if none is found, the newborn has not yet been enrolled under the policy. Here the search returns 'Member/Contract details are not found', so the newborn is not enrolled and the trainee proceeds to validate newborn eligibility.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Search → Member sub-tab is opened while this step is active. Sub-tabs start closed, so the trainee opens it deliberately. Nothing inside the sub-tab is graded: a further Search press changes the results but completes no step.
steps.hint: Click 'Search', then the 'Member' sub-tab. The results read 'Member/Contract details are not found'.
steps.checklistItem: Search for the newborn's member record

steps.name: Validate the 31-day newborn eligibility window
steps.description: Validate newborn eligibility by cross-checking the patient's DOB from the Member Information section against the DOS from the Claim Lines tab, and determine whether the DOS falls within 31 days of the DOB. If the DOS falls within 31 days of the DOB, the newborn may be eligible under the newborn coverage provision; if the DOS exceeds 31 days from the DOB, the newborn coverage provision no longer applies and enrollment must be completed before benefits can be considered. In this scenario the DOB is 09/14/2026 and the DOS is 10/20/2026 — 36 days after birth, which exceeds the 31-day newborn eligibility period — so the newborn is not eligible under the automatic newborn coverage provision, and no enrolled member record is on file. The claim therefore cannot be processed under the newborn provision, benefits cannot be applied until enrollment requirements have been met, and the claim must be denied according to the applicable business rules for non-enrolled members.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Claim Lines tab is opened again while this step is active. The 31-day arithmetic is on trust: the navigator engine has no math primitive.
steps.hint: 09/14/2026 to 10/20/2026 is 36 days — past the 31-day window for NH, and no member record exists. Deny the claim.

steps.name: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_RNBE00
steps.description: Because the newborn's date of service falls outside the state's 31-day enrollment window and no enrolled member record is on file, the claim is rejected at claim level. From the Action menu, select Deny Claim. A Deny Claim section appears below the header. Enter reject code PX_RNBE00 in the input box — the matching code appears in a dropdown list — select it and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Deny Claim panel, which dispatches the deny_claim action.
steps.hint: Action menu → Deny Claim. Enter reject code PX_RNBE00, click Submit, then confirm the pop-up.
steps.checklistItem: Deny the claim using the reject code

steps.name: Submit Deny decision
steps.description: Navigate to the Decision section in the header, select 'Deny' from the dropdown menu and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the Deny decision in the submit dialog.
steps.hint: Pick 'Deny' from the Decision dropdown in the claim header, then click Submit and confirm in the dialog.
